inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL string-function example extracts a matching numeric token with REGEXP_SUBSTR alongside replacement, position, and predicate regex functions.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored event-code audit. REGEXP_SUBSTR extracts the first ticket token from fixed messages, while a final projection combines the extracted token with NULL and no-match cases. The source literals, schema, identifiers, and comparison table are not copied.

fixture_notes: Messages contain one ticket token, two tokens, no token, and NULL. REGEXP_SUBSTR must return only the first two-letter ticket code with digits and preserve NULL for no input or no match.
determinism_notes: Message IDs, text literals, pattern, and ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE event_messages (message_id INT PRIMARY KEY, message_text VARCHAR(160) NULL)
INSERT INTO event_messages (message_id, message_text) VALUES (11, 'Deploy ticket AB-204 is queued'), (12, 'Escalation XY-9 then fallback ZZ-81'), (13, 'Routine heartbeat only'), (14, NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT message_id, message_text, REGEXP_SUBSTR(message_text, '[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]+') AS ticket_token FROM event_messages ORDER BY message_id
SELECT message_id, COALESCE(REGEXP_SUBSTR(message_text, '[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]+'), 'none') AS first_ticket FROM event_messages ORDER BY message_id
